claims.claim_text: The indexed Niver W. Beaman is a probable match to journalist Niver William Beaman, but no independent reviewed source explicitly links that journalist to OSS.
claims.evidence_excerpt: After working as a reporter in Connecticut during the 1920s, Beaman became a city editor.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A scholarly historical paper profiles the uncommon exact name Niver W. Beaman as a journalist, while a Library of Congress finding aid supplies the Niver William Beaman form.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable. The highly distinctive exact first and last name, matching middle initial, and Library of Congress full-name expansion support the match, but neither independent source mentions OSS or supplies a unique private identifier.
claims.temporal_assessment: Connecticut reporting in the 1920s is definitely pre-OSS. The paper does not date the later city-editor, New York Daily News, or Philadelphia Morning Record affiliations relative to OSS.
claims.match_notes: The identity remains probable pending review of Box 44. The archival finding aids are leads, not proof of employment or OSS service.

claims.claim_text: A probable match for Niver W. Beaman worked as a reporter in Connecticut during the 1920s; the source names no newspaper.
claims.evidence_excerpt: working as a reporter in Connecticut during the 1920s
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The scholarly appendix dates reporter work to the 1920s but does not identify the employing newspaper.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable identity based on the distinctive exact name, matching middle initial, and full-name variant; no independent reviewed source explicitly connects the journalist to OSS.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar occupation. It is not shown to be the immediate predecessor to OSS or the last civilian job before wartime service.
claims.match_notes: Published as qualified occupation-only evidence. No employer is invented, and later named newspapers are not assigned without chronology.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Corporal Robert W. Beamer is confirmed as the Army enlistee represented by the exact-name and private-identifier match in the official merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and private service identifier match across the OSS index and official Army enlistment file; the full identifier is not public.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by an exact name and unique private-identifier match. A second exact-name Army record carried a different identifier and was rejected.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official record dates Army entry to 7 January 1943; the OSS index does not supply an assignment date or predecessor role.
claims.match_notes: The identifier is retained only in the private database and masked in public outputs. Occupation code 731 is undefined in the reviewed code table, so no occupation is assigned.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Private First Class Frank C. Bean is confirmed as the Army enlistee represented by the exact private-identifier match in the official merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The private service identifier matches exactly; the merged file prints the indexed given and middle names in transposed order.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the exact unique private identifier, compatible surname and given-name elements, and enlisted Army status.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official record dates Army entry to 16 February 1943; the OSS index does not establish when Bean entered OSS.
claims.match_notes: The transposition is preserved in the citation note rather than silently treated as an exact-name match. The full identifier is private and masked publicly.

claims.claim_text: At Army entry in February 1943, Frank C. Bean's civilian occupation code grouped machinist, railway-mechanic, engine-specialist, and automobile-machinist work.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Machinist or railway mechanic, general or engine specialist
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official enlistment row carries code 475; the secondary table maps it to a broad machinist and mechanic group and names no employer.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact private-identifier match confirms that the enlistment row belongs to the indexed person despite the name-element transposition.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded to Army entry on 16 February 1943, but it does not establish exact work dates or a final named employer.
claims.match_notes: Published as the full occupation code group; the project does not select one trade or infer an employer.

research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Postwar newspaper and radio references do not establish a pre-OSS employer. The scholarly paper does not date the New York Daily News or Philadelphia Morning Record roles relative to OSS. Genealogy pages and a modern discussion forum were discovery-only and excluded.
research_attempts.research_notes: The rare name, ERIC paper, and Library of Congress finding aid support a probable identity and qualified 1920s reporter occupation. No reviewed independent source explicitly links the journalist to OSS, and no named employer meets the temporal standard. No authenticated NARA Catalog request was made.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 44, the 1943 Waterbury Republican profile, and Beaman's 1947 autobiography.
